correctness.rationale: Using the source Proposition 23, a hypothetical two-prime host is q^(2a) r^(2b). The elementary abundancy upper bound forces r=q+2 except for q=3, where r is 5 or 7. When r=q+2, exact prime-support separation in the divisor sums yields two pure prime-power equations; reducing both modulo r gives simultaneously 2^(2a+1)=-1 and 2^(2a-1)=-1, forcing r|3. The remaining (3,7) case forces 7|sigma(3^(2a)), hence ord_7(3)=6 divides an odd integer, impossible.

value.rationale: The theorem advances an explicit open problem by eliminating the entire two-prime-support regime uniformly for every odd prime q. It sharpens the source paper's best general support bound from two to three and reduces any future search for a counterexample to genuinely higher-support hosts. The proof is short, structural, and parameter-uniform rather than a finite numerical exclusion.
